n: Babylon’s chief gods, Bel and Nebo, are pictured loaded onto pack animals as the city falls—heavy cargo weighing down tired beasts. Idols have to be carried; they can’t carry anyone.

f.g: A title (“lord”) of Marduk, Babylon’s chief god.
Nabu, god of writing and wisdom, son of Marduk; his name appears in kings’ names like Nebuchadnezzar.
Things carried—loads or baggage (not wheeled vehicles).

n: The idols bow and stoop together; they can’t rescue the load—they themselves go into captivity. Ancient conquerors often carried off a defeated people’s gods.
The contrast: Israel doesn’t carry God—God has carried Israel since birth, like a parent carries a baby.

f.w: borne by me from the belly

n: Even into old age and gray hair, God will still carry and rescue His people. “I have made, and I will bear”—He takes responsibility for those He created.

f.w: I will carry, and will deliver you

n: Who could possibly compare to God?

f.w: To whom will ye liken me

n: People pour out gold and weigh silver, pay a goldsmith to make a god, then fall down and worship it—spending their wealth on something they own rather than something that owns them.

f.w: lavish gold out of the bag
f.g: Pour gold freely from their purses.

n: They hoist it on their shoulders, set it in place, and there it stands—it can’t move. People cry to it, but it can’t answer or save. Compare this with the God who carries us (verse 4).
Remember this and act like grown men; take it to heart, you rebels.

f.g: Be firm, stand strong; the Hebrew may mean “take courage” or “be ashamed.”

n: Remember what God has done in the past: He alone is God, and no one is like Him.

f.w: I am God, and there is none else

n: God announces the end from the beginning—what hasn’t happened yet. His plan will stand and He will do all He intends. Latter-day Saints see in this God’s foreknowledge and His eternal plan.

f.w: Declaring the end from the beginning

n: He calls a bird of prey from the east—Cyrus, swooping down on Babylon. What God has planned, He will carry out.

f.w: a ravenous bird from the east
f.g: A bird of prey such as an eagle; a picture of Cyrus’s swift conquest (Isaiah 41:2; 44:28).

n: God speaks to the stubborn-hearted who are far from doing right.
Yet He brings His righteousness near—salvation won’t be delayed. He will place salvation in Zion for Israel, His glory. Grace reaches even the stubborn.
